issues.description: The problem statement requires a variable named `global_count` defined as a 32-bit integer, but the provided artifacts are inconsistent: the template (helloWorld.asm) does not declare `global_count` at all, while the solution declares `global_count` using `db` (8-bit). This mismatch and the missing declaration in the template will confuse students about the required data size and prevents them from following the specification exactly.
issues.suggestedFix: Declare `global_count` as a 32-bit integer (use `dd 0`) in the template so students see the required symbol and type. Also update the solution to use `global_count dd 0` (replace `db` with `dd`) so it matches the problem statement's 32-bit requirement.

issues.description: The template uses the non-existent register name 'ecc' (add eax, ecc) while the problem statement and the solution reference the correct register 'ecx'. This inconsistent identifier for the same conceptual entity (the ECX register) creates mapping confusion and prevents successful compilation of the starter code.
issues.suggestedFix: In the template file helloWorld.asm, replace 'ecc' with the correct register name 'ecx' (i.e., change 'add eax, ecc' to 'add eax, ecx') so the code, problem text, and solution use the same identifier.
